meta.title: Naya Matter — Front-End Developer
meta.description: Portfolio of Naya Matter, a Front-End Developer specialized in React.js and Next.js.

hero.name: Naya Matter
hero.bio: Specialized in React.js and Next.js, with one year of practical training building responsive interfaces, reusable components, and REST API integrations — deployed and shipped on Vercel.

about.headline: I care how an interface holds up under real use.
paragraphs: I'm currently a Front-End Developer at NVT in As-Suwayda, building with React and Next.js. Before that, a year as a developer intern at Vica Web Solution — building reusable component libraries, wiring REST APIs into production frontends, and testing endpoints until the data actually behaved. Every project shipped to Vercel.
Before that, a degree in Information Engineering — Artificial Intelligence from Damascus University.

skills.headline: What I actually reach for when I'm building.

experience.headline: Where I've worked, and what came before it.

points: Building front-end features with React and Next.js.
Responsive React.js and Tailwind CSS applications
Reusable components and REST API integration
SQL and NoSQL data — PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB
Coursework in algorithms, data structures, and software engineering.

projects.headline: Recent work, from client sites to internal platforms.

ftt.name: FTT
ftt.summary: Marketing site for a training company with an authenticated dashboard behind it — the public pages, gallery, and application flow are all editable by staff.
highlights: Public site, gallery, and multi-step application form
Dashboard with sortable tables and drag-to-reorder content
SEO handled at the framework level — sitemap and robots routes

cvg.name: CVG
cvg.summary: Agency site where every section is content-managed. Hero, services, projects, values, process, contact, and footer each have a matching dashboard editor.
highlights: Nine independently editable page sections, one CMS screen each
Scroll and reveal choreography built with GSAP
Typed service layer over a shared HTTP client

inventory.name: Inventory
inventory.summary: Multi-store inventory dashboard — stock levels, movement charts, and per-store breakdowns. Runs entirely on seeded data, so it is safe to demo end to end.
highlights: Interactive area charts and summary cards over store data
Filterable, column-sortable data tables
Auth flow and protected dashboard routes

task-system.name: Task System
task-system.summary: Company-wide work platform: workspaces, projects, kanban boards, tickets, help requests, time clocking, and a weighted staff rating system, all under role-based access.
highlights: Drag-and-drop kanban across projects and workspaces
Live updates over WebSockets with Laravel Echo and Pusher
Roles and permissions gating every route
Clock in/out with session and record history

courses.name: Courses
courses.summary: A full learning platform, and the largest thing I have shipped — around 500 source files split across an admin console and a learner-facing app.
highlights: Admin: course, video, audio, quiz, evaluation, and user management
Learner: enrolment, quizzes, progress tracking, schedule, feedback
Configurable attention-score engine with live preview and history
Certificate generation to PDF, rich-text authoring with TinyMCE

web2api-ui.name: Web2API UI
web2api-ui.summary: Chat front-end for an AI gateway. Streaming responses render as they arrive, including code, math, diagrams, and CJK text.
highlights: Token-by-token streaming with sticky-to-bottom scroll
Rich message rendering — Shiki highlighting, math, Mermaid diagrams
Node-graph views built on React Flow
Live token accounting against model context limits

lumina-connector.name: Lumina Connector
lumina-connector.summary: A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that links a user's Gemini session to Lumina in one click, replacing a manual cookie-copying step.
highlights: One-click session hand-off, cookies held in memory only
Self-hosted private distribution with automatic updates
Go native-messaging host performs on-disk updates
No-admin installers for Windows and macOS

pizza-dashboard.name: Pizza Dashboard
pizza-dashboard.summary: A multi-store operations platform for a restaurant chain — staff break tracking, a full cleaning inspection and scoring system, and an inventory counting workflow, all under one roof.
highlights: Cleaning Chart System — daily checklists, inspection grading, and a scored store leaderboard
Inventory counting via single-use employee links, no account required to submit
Automatic unit-conversion chains (case → box → LB) per catalog item
CSV and themed PNG exports for every store report
